topic: Holiday couch slouching: long TV sessions and your back

slides.headline: Couch marathons leaving your back stiff?
slides.sub: Holiday TV is fine. Your back just likes a change of scene.

slides.title: Slouching isn't the villain
slides.body: No single position is wrong for your back. The trouble is staying in one shape for three episodes straight. Comfort usually comes from changing position, not finding a perfect one.

slides.title: Move between episodes
slides.body: When an episode ends, stand up, walk to the kitchen, reach both arms overhead and do five gentle back bends. One or two minutes every 30 to 45 minutes adds up.

slides.title: Support it, then swap it
slides.body: A cushion behind your lower back, feet on the floor or an ottoman, and the screen at eye level all help. Then switch sides, sit cross-legged or lie on the floor for a while.

slides.title: Balance screen days with walks
slides.body: Days that are all couch can leave backs feeling stiff by evening. A morning walk or swim and a few minutes of easy stretching tend to make the evening viewing more comfortable.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: Pain that wakes you and doesn't ease with moving, numbness around the groin, changes to bladder or bowel control, leg weakness or fever deserve a prompt check with your GP.

slides.headline: Back stiff after the break?
slides.body: Our chiropractors look at how you move and combine hands-on care with practical exercises for the year ahead. Book online via the link in bio.

caption:
Binge-watching over the break? Your back would like an intermission.

There's no perfect way to sit on the couch, and slouching isn't harmful in itself. What tends to make backs stiff is staying in one shape for hours.

Try this during your next series: stand up between episodes, walk to the kitchen, reach overhead and do a few gentle back bends. Use a cushion behind your lower back, swap sides now and then, and balance couch days with a morning walk or swim.

Pain that wakes you at night, numbness around the groin, bladder or bowel changes or leg weakness need a prompt GP check.
